nexusClaim.associationBasis: Authoring registers this relationship only as the population-level association the located adult literature supports and deliberately not beyond it: a 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 eligible studies (random-effects model) found bruxism associated with temporomandibular disorders at pooled odds ratio 2.25 (95 percent CI 1.94-2.56), with awake bruxism at 2.51 (95 percent CI 2.02-2.99) and sleep bruxism at 2.06 (95 percent CI 1.82-2.30) (PMID 37474733), while a 2017 systematic review of 39 studies found 33 reporting a positive relation and 6 not, graded the evidence low to moderate, and reported that polysomnographically diagnosed studies were LESS conclusive than survey or clinical diagnosis (PMID 27796166). The claim is group-level association: the pooled studies are observational and predominantly cross-sectional, and the meta-analysis's conclusion that bruxism increases the likelihood of developing temporomandibular disorders in the future is an inference beyond those designs. Direction cannot be established from the located evidence because temporomandibular pain and dysfunction themselves alter masticatory behavior, and the juvenile null registered as this edge's counterweight (PMID 9758394) is reconciled only as a matter of age scope, not as support. The association is conditioned on how bruxism and the temporomandibular disorder are measured.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of temporomandibular joint disorders is established for any individual, and the direction is explicitly unresolved: every located anchor is cross-sectional, case-control or review-level, so nothing in the located evidence can separate bruxism loading the joint from temporomandibular pain and dysfunction driving parafunctional behavior, and the two conditions share plausible third factors (psychological stress and anxiety, sleep fragmentation, medication, occlusal and dental factors) that the located designs do not control. Bruxism is itself the umbrella identity (awake and sleep) while the strongest pooled estimates are type-specific, and the juvenile null shows a population in which the association was NOT observed. Individual claims require independently documented bruxism by clinical dental examination with its awake-versus-sleep phenotype (wear facets, masticatory muscle findings, partner-reported grinding), a separately established temporomandibular disorder diagnosis with examination and imaging where indicated, a dated chronology that can speak to direction, and exclusion of medication-induced bruxism, sleep-disordered breathing, trauma, occlusal and dental treatment effects, and other competing causes before any attribution.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized mechanical loading pathway: sustained parafunctional masticatory muscle activity — awake clenching and sleep grinding — is held to impose repetitive load on the temporomandibular joint and its musculature, plausibly through masticatory co-contraction, joint compression and disc loading, producing or aggravating myofascial pain, arthralgia and joint changes; no located anchor isolates that cascade in an individual and the reverse pathway is at least as plausible, so the vector is stated as hypothesized rather than established.
causalMechanism.secondaryVector: Where temporomandibular pain and dysfunction already exist, altered motor behavior, guarding and pain-related avoidance can themselves drive or sustain parafunctional activity, and shared third factors (psychological stress, sleep disturbance, medication such as SSRIs and stimulants, occlusal and dental factors) can produce both conditions; the located designs do not separate these routes from the claimed direction.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY on one adult systematic review and meta-analysis, one adult systematic review, and one juvenile longitudinal cohort registered as an explicit counterweight, and deliberately not beyond them. The pooled adult association is moderate and method-conditioned: pooled odds ratio 2.25 (95 percent CI 1.94-2.56) across 20 studies, awake bruxism 2.51 (2.02-2.99) and sleep bruxism 2.06 (1.82-2.30) (PMID 37474733), while the earlier 39-study review found 33 positive and 6 negative studies, graded the evidence low to moderate with design shortcomings and low bruxism-diagnostic sensitivity, and reported that polysomnographically diagnosed studies were less conclusive than survey or clinical diagnosis (PMID 27796166). The counterweight is the ME-34 anchor: 150 juvenile bruxers aged 6 to 9 followed five years, of whom only 17 retained the habit, concluding that juvenile bruxing was self-limiting, does not progress to adult bruxism and appeared unrelated to TMJ symptoms (PMID 9758394). The signed ME-34 reopening reconciles the two as an AGE-SCOPE reconciliation only: the juvenile null and the adult association measure different populations and can both stand; neither is evidence about the other's population. Direction is unresolved and is carried on the face of the edge — the edge does not assert that bruxism causes temporomandibular joint disease in any individual, and the association is as consistent with pain-driven parafunction as with loading-driven disease. No located anchor establishes individual causation or aggravation, none is a prospective incidence cohort with an established temporal order, and the three anchors remain unverified pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md; this suggestion, its adjacency node and the registry lockstep landed together on 2026-10-04 under Stage 3c of the signed design.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Direction and design: every located anchor is cross-sectional, case-control or review-level, so no temporal order between bruxism and temporomandibular disorders is established and the bidirectional reading cannot be resolved; the pooled association cannot be separated from the possibility that temporomandibular pain and dysfunction drive parafunctional behavior rather than the reverse. Measurement: bruxism was ascertained by polysomnography, clinical examination, self-report or screening instrument across the pooled studies, the located reviews report the association depends on the diagnostic method, and the polysomnographically diagnosed subset was the least conclusive; the umbrella identity spans awake and sleep bruxism while the strongest pooled estimates are type-specific. Population and age scope: the pooled positive association is adult, while the counterweight null is juvenile (ages 6 to 9), and no located anchor bridges the age transition or studies the juvenile relationship against modern diagnostic criteria. Overlapping literature: the 2017 review's 39 studies and the 2023 meta-analysis's 20 studies draw on substantially overlapping primary studies, so they are not independent confirmations of one another, and the meta-analysis's future-development conclusion outruns its cross-sectional designs. No individual-level exposure-response: the located evidence reports group-level odds ratios and prevalences, and no anchor quantifies parafunction frequency, duration or intensity against individual temporomandibular outcomes.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Temporomandibular disorder arising independently of bruxism — trauma, arthritis and other joint disease, disc displacement, joint hypermobility, dental or occlusal treatment effects, or idiopathic myofascial pain.

Medication-induced bruxism (SSRIs and other antidepressants, stimulants, antipsychotics) or medication-related jaw symptoms within the treatment timeline, producing or amplifying the parafunction rather than arising from it.

Shared substrate: psychological stress, anxiety and sleep disturbance driving BOTH bruxism and temporomandibular disorders, which the located designs cannot separate from a bruxism-to-disorder pathway.
Sleep-disordered breathing and other sleep disorders as arousal sources for sleep bruxism and for morning jaw symptoms, independent of any bruxism-to-joint pathway.
Reverse causal order: temporomandibular pain and dysfunction driving altered masticatory behavior and parafunction, which the cross-sectional designs cannot exclude.

Age-scope mismatch: applying the adult pooled association to juvenile populations or the juvenile null to adults, which the ME-34 age-scope reconciliation makes impermissible without population-specific evidence.

suggestions.rationale: Authoring executes the signed ME-34 reopening (docs/catalog-identity-migration-design-2026-09-29.md, Stage 3c) for the bruxism-awake-sleep to tmj-disorder route only, on the ordinary draft path because both mappings are drafts, and lands together with the adjacency node and the registry lockstep on 2026-10-04. The signed disposition is an AGE-SCOPE reconciliation: the original ME-34 rejection rested on PMID 9758394, a juvenile cohort (150 bruxers aged 6 to 9, 126 re-examined after five years, only 17 retaining the habit) that found juvenile bruxing self-limiting and appeared unrelated to TMJ symptoms, while the adult evidence located since is meta-analytically positive — bruxism associated with temporomandibular disorders at pooled odds ratio 2.25 (95 percent CI 1.94-2.56), awake 2.51 (2.02-2.99) and sleep 2.06 (1.82-2.30) across 20 eligible studies (PMID 37474733) — and consistent with the earlier 39-study review (33 positive, 6 negative, quality low to moderate, polysomnographic evidence least conclusive; PMID 27796166). The two measure different populations and can both stand; the juvenile null is carried as an explicit counterweight rather than discarded, and this edge registers evidence about adults only. The edge does not assert that bruxism causes temporomandibular joint disease in any individual: direction is unresolved and disclosed, the located designs are observational, the association is as consistent with pain-driven parafunction as with loading-driven disease, and diagnosis-method conditioning is carried on the face. The ME-34 rejection itself remains on the record, annotated as superseded as to outcome only; no other ME-34 conclusion is reopened. The original rejection named tmj-dysfunction; under Leg C of the signed design the canonical TMJ identity is tmj-disorder (tmj-dysfunction is a quarantined pointer), and this route is authored to the canonical identity, where the sibling batch-91 edge ptsd to bruxism-awake-sleep keeps its own ME-34 boundary without contradiction — when both windows exist, CRG reports ptsd to bruxism to tmj chains against any future direct ptsd to tmj-disorder claim, and none is proposed here. Window discipline: this is the only registered window from bruxism-awake-sleep; a future TMJ-first window (tmj-disorder to bruxism-awake-sleep) would require a fresh npm run audit:crg adjudication and is not authored. The route's anchors (PMID 37474733, PMID 27796166, PMID 9758394) were confirmed absent from the registry and cleared by source-status preflight with zero blocking flags on 2026-10-04; they enter verified:false pending qualified-human citation verification under docs/citation-verification-sop.md, and the relationship row and the three source entities were registered in lockstep with this suggestion on 2026-10-04.
evidenceGaps: Direction unresolved by design: every located anchor is observational (cross-sectional, case-control or review-level), no anchor establishes that bruxism precedes temporomandibular disorders in incident cohorts, and the association is as consistent with pain-driven parafunction as with bruxism-driven loading.

Diagnosis-method conditioning: bruxism was ascertained by polysomnography, clinical examination, self-report or screening instrument across the pooled studies, the located reviews report the association depends on the diagnostic method, and the polysomnographically diagnosed subset was the LEAST conclusive (PMID 27796166; PMID 37474733).

Population and age scope: the pooled positive association is adult, while the counterweight null is juvenile (ages 6 to 9, self-limiting bruxing that did not progress to adult bruxism; PMID 9758394); neither population is evidence about the other, and no located anchor bridges the age transition.

Overlapping underlying literature: the 2017 review's 39 studies and the 2023 meta-analysis's 20 studies draw on substantially overlapping primary studies, so they are not independent confirmations of one another; the meta-analysis's conclusion about developing temporomandibular disorders in the future outruns its cross-sectional designs.

No individual-level exposure-response: the located evidence reports group-level odds ratios and prevalences; no anchor quantifies parafunction frequency, duration or intensity against individual temporomandibular outcomes, and the awake-versus-sleep components cannot be pooled without the type-specific estimates.

sourceReferences.citation: Mortazavi N, Tabatabaei AH, Mohammadi M, Rajabi A. Is bruxism associated with temporomandibular joint disorders? A systematic review and meta-analysis. Evid Based Dent. 2023 Sep;24(3):144. doi:10.1038/s41432-023-00911-6. PMID 37474733.
sourceReferences.note: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 20 eligible studies (searches through March 2022; Newcastle-Ottawa quality assessment; random-effects model), registered as this edge's PRIMARY adult association anchor: bruxism associated with temporomandibular disorders at pooled odds ratio 2.25 (95 percent CI 1.94-2.56), awake bruxism 2.51 (2.02-2.99) and sleep bruxism 2.06 (1.82-2.30). LIMITATIONS CARRIED: the pooled studies are observational and predominantly cross-sectional, so the association is method-conditioned and cannot establish direction; the abstract's both-types pooled estimate is printed as OR 2.17 with a confidence interval of 2.30-3.05 that excludes its own point estimate, an apparent typographical error in the published abstract, and it is not relied on here; the authors' conclusion that bruxism increases the likelihood of developing temporomandibular disorders in the future outruns the cross-sectional designs. Mapping approval is not citation verification; this source enters verified:false pending separate qualified-human citation review.

LIMITATIONS CARRIED: the review's 39 primary studies overlap substantially with the 2023 meta-analysis's 20 studies, so the two reviews are not independent evidence sets. sourceReferences.note: Five-year longitudinal juvenile cohort, registered as this edge's EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT and as the ME-34 rejection's anchor: 150 bruxers aged 6 to 9 examined for oral parafunctions and TMJ symptoms, 126 re-examined after five years, only 17 retaining the bruxing habit; symptoms reduced with age and the authors concluded juvenile bruxing was self-limiting, did not progress to adult bruxism and appeared unrelated to TMJ symptoms.
